predecessors.name: Third Dynasty of Ur
predecessors.text: Eshnunna and its Diyala district, an Ur III province under governors such as Urguedinna and Ituria

successors.name: Babylonia
successors.text: Eshnunna and its Diyala, Arrapha and Euphrates lands

ledger.x: c. 2026 BC: Shu-iliya makes Eshnunna independent of Ur. "Shu-iliya drops the Ur III calendar, calls himself lugal, and is listed as gaining independence from Ibbi-Sin"; the page: "in 2026 BC got rid of the Ur III calendar". Year from the page; the land is my reading (Tell Asmar and its district). The…

c. 2011 BC (derived): Subartu seizes Eshnunna. The page has Eshnunna independent as the state of Warum "for about 15 years" after 2026, then "Subartu briefly seizes the city"; 2026 minus 15 gives 2011, the page dates no seizure.
c. 2010 BC: Ishbi-Erra of Isin "defeats Subartu and installs Nur-ahum". The page does not call Nur-ahum a vassal of Isin.

c. 1900 BC: "Warassa (Warissa) conquers Ishur, Tutub, and Nerebtum (Kiti, at Tell Ishchali)". The Ipiq-Adad II page has Ipiq-Adad II "defeated Sin-abushu of Nerebtum" c. 1828 and annexing Tutub, so the 1900 conquest did not hold, or the pages disagree; the land (the lower Diyala near Baghdad) is my reading.
ledger.cp: Ishur, Tutub and Nerebtum (city-states on the lower Diyala)

ledger.x: c. 1855 BC: Ipiq-Adad II takes Shaduppum. The page has the campaign against Aminum c. 1857, "attempting to seize Shaduppum" (Tell Harmal): "first defeated, but won the second confrontation two years later"; the Dadusha page counts Shaduppum among the lands "brought under Eshnunna by his father, Ipiq-Adad II".

c. 1828 BC: Ipiq-Adad II takes Arrapha. He "took Arrapha to the north" and then defeated Sin-abushu of Nerebtum "to consolidate the Diyala region", annexing Uzarlulu and Tutub in the same campaign. Arrapha is Kirkuk (my reading).

c. 1828 BC (bridged to the Arrapha campaign): Rapiqum, Suhum and Me-Turan. The page lists them undated: "Rapiqum was taken, his first city on the Euphrates", "Eshnunna expanded up the Euphrates to the Suhum region, bordering Mari", "Me-Turan was taken"; the reign is c. 1862-1818 and the page dates no conquest. The…

c. 1776 BC: Ibal-pi-El II seizes Mahazum. Year-name 4: "Ibal-pi-El seized the land of Mahazum", a district on the Diyala River; the page gives no coordinates, so the whole Diyala governorate is shown as a stand-in.

c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna occupies Assur. "In c. 1772 BC, the new king of Eshnunna, Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom, occupying Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare". The Eshnunna page puts the taking of Assur and Ekallatum under Ibal-pi-El II without a year.
c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna seizes Subat-Enlil. "... before seizing Shamshi-Adad's old capital at Shubut-Enlil." The Eshnunna page: Eshnunna "takes Shubat-Enlil". Mirrors the assyria loss.

c. 1767 BC: Elam takes Eshnunna. "Elam, under Siwe-palar-huppak, takes Eshnunna in Zimri-Lim's 9th year"; the Ibal-pi-El II page: around 1767 he led a coalition against Eshnunna, "conquering it and imposed direct rule from his sukkal Kudu-zulush in Susa", and has Ibal-pi-El II killed c. 1765 (it calls its own dating…

c. 1767 BC (bridged): the occupation of Assur ends. The pages do not say when Eshnunna left Assur and Subat-Enlil; Eshnunna was conquered by Elam around 1767 and Ishme-Dagan I (d. c. 1765) "retained control only of Ekallatum" (Old Assyrian period). Mirrors the assyria dossier.
c. 1767 BC (bridged): Subat-Enlil is no longer Eshnunna's. The pages say nothing about Subat-Enlil after c. 1772; shown as lost with the Elamite conquest. Page silent.

c. 1764 BC: Silli-Sin is "installed by Eshnunnian troops" and reigns c. 1764-1756; "He makes a treaty with Hammurabi and marries Hammurabi's daughter." The elam dossier (me-01) ends its occupation at -1760 ("Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites").
1762 BC (Hammurabi year 31): "the Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna".

wars.name: Ipiq-Adad II against Aminum and Shaduppum
wars.outcome: Ipiq-Adad II was first defeated, "but won the second confrontation two years later"; Shaduppum was Eshnunna's afterwards (Dadusha page).

wars.name: Elamite invasion in Ipiq-Adad II's reign
wars.outcome: "Invaded again, this time by the Elamites around 1823 BC"; the page does not say how it ended.

wars.name: Qabra campaign with Shamshi-Adad I
wars.outcome: "Around 1781 BC, the coalition with Dadusha and Shamshi-Adad I besieged the city"; Qabarum became a provincial centre in Shamshi-Adad's kingdom, not Eshnunna's.

wars.name: Eshnunna against Ishme-Dagan I and Mari
wars.outcome: Eshnunna occupied Assur, Ekallatum, Qattara and Subat-Enlil c.

wars.name: Elamite conquest of Eshnunna
wars.outcome: Siwe-Palar-Khuppak "conquering it and imposed direct rule from his sukkal Kudu-zulush in Susa"; Ibal-pi-El II killed c.

wars.name: Babylonian occupation of Eshnunna
wars.outcome: "The Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna" in Hammurabi's year 31 (1762 BC).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the city and the districts the pages name.
